channel.title: Guarana blog
channel.description: Engineering notes from Guarana, an open-source Switch 2 emulator fork for integrated GPUs: what we measured, how, and what is still in progress.

item.title: How a shader fix took Hyrule Field from 14.8 to 22.8 fps on an Intel Arc iGPU
item.dc:creator: Guarana contributors
item.description: How EDEN_NX2_GM=11 cut a foliage draw from 15.7 to 5.8 ms and took Hyrule Field from 14.8 to 22.8 game fps on an Arc 140T iGPU, and where the proof stops.

item.title: Why 16.67 ms is hard: frame pacing and frame generation on a 120 Hz OLED
item.dc:creator: Guarana contributors
item.description: Why motion stuttered with frame generation on: forced FIFO, a present thread not locked to vblank, fixed-fraction prediction, and the fix in progress.

item.title: Booting a Switch 2 emulator in half the time: what the boot marks found
item.dc:creator: Guarana contributors
item.description: Boot timing marks show about 11 s of a 24.7 s boot is Vulkan instance creation. What the marks log, what is being cut next, and how to measure your own.

item.title: An emulator built for AI agents: AGENTS.md, an MCP server that drives the game, and free CI builds per PR
item.dc:creator: Guarana contributors
item.description: Rules in AGENTS.md, scoped agent-ready issues, a loopback MCP server that drives a running game, and a CI build for every pull request. How it all fits.
